morgan: Hey team — overnight we saw a ~4x spike in GPU OOMs around 02:15 UTC. Initial perf sampling points at KV prefix cache fragmentation + TTL churn as the likely culprit. Posting the sample dump and a quick hypothesis. :thinking:

morgan: sample dump (trimmed):
```
kv_cache_stats {
  total_keys: 12_430_982
  avg_key_size: 384B
  median_ttl: 22s
  ttl_90: 4m12s
  free_segments: 1_432 (many tiny <=256B)
  slab_waste_bytes: 1.1GB
  evictions/sec: 1_200 -> spikes to 11_000 during incident
  gpu_alloc_failures: 423 (peak)
}
```

morgan: Hypothesis: a mix of lots of short-lived small keys and a few large pinned keys is causing the slab allocator to fragment on the GPU side; when the runtime tries to batch larger generation requests kernel selection picks a variant that needs contiguous GPU KV space, allocation fails, and we OOM. TTL oscillation (many keys with ~0-60s TTL) amplifies the free-list churn.

raj: Can you repro locally with loadgen? If we can get a deterministic repro we can test defrag/compaction patches. Also what's the CPU cache size vs GPU cache size?

morgan: repro looks doable. I ran kv-sim with a mixed workload (zipf=1.1, key_size_dist: 70% small 64-512B, 25% medium 1-8KB, 5% large 16-64KB, ttl-dist heavy mass at <60s). Current prod config: CPU cache ~12GB, GPU pinned cache ~8GB.

sofia: quick histogram from prod sampling (last 24h):
```
key_size_hist: [<256B: 68% , 256-1KB: 18%, 1KB-8KB: 9%, >8KB: 5%]
ttl_buckets: [<10s: 42%, 10-60s: 30%, 1-10m: 20%, >10m: 8%]
access_pattern: mostly read-prefetch on short prefixes, bursts of long-prefix generation every 10-20s
```

kevin: TL;DR: short-lived keys + skewed size distribution -> many tiny free blocks. Our LRU eviction is global across CPU/GPU which causes ping-pong of items between tiers. Two proposals: (A) decouple GPU LRU for pinned allocation (keep a small contiguous reserve) and (B) add a periodic compaction pass during low load that coalesces adjacent free segments.

taylor: +1 on decoupling. Also batching heuristics are hurting: when we build large batches we choose kernels optimized for large KV footprint; but if the batch includes a lot of small-key requests we should prefer a kernel that tolerates fragmented KV layout (even if slightly slower). We can add a pre-batch sampler to estimate needed contiguous space.

raj: Experiment plan I suggest:
1) repro load: `kv-sim --clients 600 --zipf 1.1 --ttl-mix small:0.7,med:0.25,large:0.05 --burst 20s` (morgan to own)
2) patch runtime: add small contiguous reserve on GPU (1GB) + toggle to decouple LRU between cpu/gpu (kevin)
3) add compaction probe: compact when GPU utilization < 40% and free_segments > 1k (sofia)
4) change batching heuristic: run sample-based kernel selector that favors fragmentation-tolerant kernels when small-key fraction > 0.6 (taylor)
5) run canary for 6h and compare evictions/sec, slab_waste_bytes, and gpu_alloc_failures (perf-bot will collect)

perf-bot: ack — will track metrics: `evictions/sec`, `gpu_alloc_failures`, `slab_waste_bytes`, `avg_alloc_latency` and post hourly.

morgan: Quick patch I tried locally: added a compaction pass that scans free list and merges adjacent segments; simple heuristic: run every 60s if free_segments_count > 1000. Local run reduced slab_waste by ~430MB and evictions peak by ~32%. Patch:```
// pseudo
if (free_segments > 1000 && gpu_util < 0.4) compact_free_list();
```

sofia: Nice. Two caveats: compaction has CPU/GPU sync cost — we must ensure it doesn't block the fast path. Suggest implementing as a cooperative async job that yields after N merges. Also TTL bumping: for some short prefixes we might set a min-ttl=5s to reduce churn. Worth testing but can affect cold-hit latency.

kevin: Also consider a tiny slab-class rebalancer: move small keys to dedicated small-key slabs (on GPU) to avoid fragmentation from large keys. That plus a small reserve should help.

taylor: I can prototype the kernel-selector sampler this afternoon — essentially sample 5% of a batch's prefixes, compute small_key_fraction, pick kernel A (frag-tolerant) if > threshold else kernel B (fast contiguous). Should be cheap.

raj: Owners: morgan (repro + compaction), kevin (reserve + slab-classes), taylor (kernel sampler), sofia (canary metrics + TTL experiments). Let's aim for an internal canary by EOD tomorrow.

morgan: Cool. I'll push a small compaction branch and run the repro with `kv-sim` now. Will post results in this thread. :rocket:

sofia: Thanks — if anyone sees a production spike in the next 12h please ping @oncall.eyes :eyes:

perf-bot: scheduled job created: `kv-frag-canary-180124` — posting hourly metrics to #eng-runtime/canaries.

kevin: one more note — if compaction reduces alloc failures but slows small requests unacceptably we can make compaction adaptive (only run when tail-latency < SLO).

morgan: Agree. I'll include tail-latency gating in the canary.

sofia: ack, thanks all. :thumbsup:
